We need answer only JSON object with declaration, implementation, supporting_objects. Need implement CODESYS FB_Task. Need exact interface names/types. Need define referenced DUTs. State enum perhaps DUT E_TaskState. Function block declaration with VAR_INPUT Start Stop AtExit Jam Reset : BOOL; VAR_OUTPUT Belt Complete Fault : BOOL; VAR state : E_TaskState := E_TaskState.IDLE; maybe no others. Need implementation one transition per scan. Need ensure initial state IDLE and outputs false. Need handle priority.

Need think semantics carefully. At scan: sample inputs, pre-state q. Execute at most one transition. Outputs based on resulting state? Requirements: Jam forces FAULT from any state; Belt and Complete FALSE there. With Jam FALSE, Reset returns any state to IDLE. Without Reset, FAULT latched. Stop aborts non-fault cycle to IDLE. In IDLE accept Start only if AtExit FALSE and enter MOVING. In MOVING AtExit enters COMPLETE. COMPLETE held until Reset or Stop; Start alone does not clear. Belt TRUE only in MOVING, Complete only in COMPLETE Fault only in FAULT. Execute at most one state transition per scan.

Need interpret priority. Safety priority: Jam, Reset when Jam FALSE, Latched fault, Stop, Normal transition. Need implement maybe:

IF Jam THEN state := FAULT;
ELSIF Reset THEN state := IDLE;
ELSIF state = FAULT THEN state := FAULT; (latched)
ELSIF Stop THEN state := IDLE;
ELSE
  CASE state OF
    IDLE: IF Start AND NOT AtExit THEN state := MOVING; END_IF
    MOVING: IF AtExit THEN state := COMPLETE; END_IF
    COMPLETE: // hold
    FAULT: // already handled
  END_CASE
END_IF

Then outputs:
Belt := (state = MOVING);
Complete := (state = COMPLETE);
Fault := (state = FAULT);

Question: When Jam true in MOVING, state FAULT same scan Belt false. Good. When Reset true and Jam false in FAULT, state IDLE same scan outputs false. If Reset true in MOVING? Priority Reset returns any state to IDLE if Jam false. Yes. If Stop true in COMPLETE -> IDLE. If Stop true in MOVING -> IDLE. If Stop true in IDLE, state IDLE. If Start true and AtExit true in IDLE, no transition (stays IDLE). Good. If AtExit true in MOVING and Start etc, enters COMPLETE (unless Reset/Stop/Jam). Good.

Need consider "Without Reset, FAULT is latched." Our ELSIF state=FAULT before Stop ensures Stop cannot clear fault. Good. Reset when Jam false clears fault. If Jam true and Reset true, Jam priority sets FAULT. Good.

Need "Reset returns any state to IDLE" with Jam FALSE. Does Reset in IDLE clear? stays IDLE. Good.

Need at most one transition. Our if/elsif ensures one assignment. CASE one.

Potential issue: "Stop aborts a non-fault cycle to IDLE" if Stop in COMPLETE clears complete, yes. If Stop and Start in IDLE, Stop priority over normal, stays IDLE. Good.

Need output Fault only in FAULT. In Jam true when previous IDLE, state set FAULT and Fault true same scan. Good.

(

    MOVING,
    COMPLETE,
    FAULT
);
END_TYPE

Need implement:
IF Jam THEN
    state := E_TaskState.FAULT;
ELSIF Reset THEN
    state := E_TaskState.IDLE;
ELSIF state = E_TaskState.FAULT THEN
    state := E_TaskState.FAULT;  // maybe no assignment needed, but "execute transition"? Could leave. But latching is no transition. But to avoid transition count? It's an assignment same state. Could omit? Need ensure Stop doesn't clear fault. If state=FAULT and no jam/reset, then we can just do nothing, not even assignment. But ELSIF state=FAULT THEN ;? ST empty branch maybe. Better:
ELSIF state = E_TaskState.FAULT THEN
    ; // latched
ELSIF Stop THEN
...
But empty statement? CODESYS allows ;? Maybe. Or state := E_TaskState.FAULT; same value. It is not a state transition because same. Fine. But priority "latched fault" before Stop. Good.
ELSIF Stop THEN
    state := E_TaskState.IDLE;
ELSE
    CASE state OF
        E_TaskState.IDLE:
            IF Start AND NOT AtExit THEN
                state := E_TaskState.MOVING;
            END_IF;
        E_TaskState.MOVING:
            IF AtExit THEN
                state := E_TaskState.COMPLETE;
            END_IF;
        E_TaskState.COMPLETE:
            ; // hold
        E_TaskState.FAULT:
            ; // handled
    END_CASE;
END_IF;

Belt := (state = E_TaskState.MOVING);
Complete := (state = E_TaskState.COMPLETE);
Fault := (state = E_TaskState.FAULT);

Potential issue: If Reset true and state IDLE and Start true, Reset priority returns IDLE and prevents start. Requirement safety priority Reset before normal, yes. If Reset true and AtExit true etc, no start. Good.

Potential issue: "Reset returns any state to IDLE" but output Fault false same scan. Yes.

Need maybe "Fault only in FAULT" and state is set to FAULT if Jam. Good.
